extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, agents, and IP professionals seeking information on ARIPO filing, prosecution, and online search tools
extracted.subtask_short: ARIPO patent filing and search guidance
extracted.subtask_description: Practical and legal information about filing, protection, and searching patents (and related rights) under the ARIPO/Harare Protocol framework, plus how to use ARIPO online registers and gazettes. Includes jurisdictional coverage, PCT interactions, available IP rights, and online search tips.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harare Protocol empowerment
rubrics_metrics.description: The Harare Protocol empowers the ARIPO Office to receive and process patent and industrial design applications on behalf of States party to the protocol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protocol was adopted in December 1982, entered into force in April 1984, and (as amended in 1993) incorporates the PCT. It enables ARIPO to act on behalf of contracting states for patents, industrial designs and utility models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of ARIPO patent protection (patents, designs, utility models)
rubrics_metrics.description: ARIPO can grant patents and register industrial designs as well as utility models on behalf of the contracting states under the Harare Protocol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Particularities: the Protocol provides centralized filing/registration on behalf of member states (except where members are not party to the Protocol). Applicants should confirm whether the target member state is party to the Harare Protocol before relying on ARIPO procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership and Protocol coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Current ARIPO members: Botswana, Cape Verde, eSwatini, Gambia, Ghana, Kenya, Lesotho, Liberia, Malawi, Mauritius (not member of the Harare Protocol), Mozambique, Namibia, Rwanda, Sào Tomé and Príncipe, Seychelles, Sierra Leone, Somalia (not member of the Harare Protocol), Sudan, Tanzania, Uganda, Zambia and Zimbabwe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Harare Protocol is in force in all 22 member states except Mauritius and Somalia. Applicants must check whether a given member state is party to the Protocol to determine ARIPO applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interaction with the PCT
rubrics_metrics.description: With the exception of Somalia, all ARIPO members are also Contracting Parties to the Patent Cooperation Treaty (PCT); ARIPO itself can be designated under the PCT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: eSwatini can be designated only via the ARIPO. The 1993 amendment to the Harare Protocol incorporated the PCT—applicants should be aware of PCT-ARIPO filing/designation pathways and any country-specific designation rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online Patent Register language and legal-status retrieval
rubrics_metrics.description: The online patent register has an English interface and allows retrieval of information on Legal Status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users can find Legal Status entries such as 'Withdrawal' (example: Application Number AP/P/2000/001992). Confirm that the interface language and legal-status labels meet your needs when checking prosecution histories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Searchable fields in the online register
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent register can be searched by PCT Application/Publication Number, by Applicant/Inventor Name, and by Priority Data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PCT Application/Publication Number searches can be done using formats like, e.g., 'PCT Application No.' PCT/US99/09463. Use the specified formats to improve search accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: ARIPO JOURNAL (Online Gazette) availability and format
rubrics_metrics.description: The online gazette is searchable by number and downloadable in PDF format, published monthly in English, with current coverage from 2015 to present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the monthly ARIPO JOURNAL for official notices; older issues prior to 2015 may not be available via this interface.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication Server legal-status searching
rubrics_metrics.description: The Publication Server allows alternative searching of the ARIPO JOURNAL by Legal Status (e.g., patent application abandoned, filed, pending grant, patent granted, patent assigned).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Legal Status filters to find items by prosecution outcome. Example legal-status label: 'Withdrawal'. This is useful for tracking the lifecycle of applications and granted patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secondary patent database on WIPO Publish
rubrics_metrics.description: A second patent database including patents of ARIPO and of ARIPO’s members is built on the WIPO Publish platform.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This WIPO Publish interface allows selecting between a search limited to the most frequently used fields and a broader search across many fields using a slider button; some broader fields may be optional/left empty. Use the broader search when needed, but be aware of optional fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on national IP rights search coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: On the search page of the online register, you can choose between ARIPO and national IP rights, but the latter is currently loading and a search gives no results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When searching for national IP rights via the ARIPO interface, verify whether national registers are actually available; incomplete loading may mean you need to consult national offices directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Member States’ Journals availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Member States’ Journals are available for download but coverage is partial (currently covering Kenya, Mozambique, Rwanda, Sào Tomé and Príncipe and Tanzania only).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For national-level journal notices, check whether the specific member state's journal is present in the ARIPO portal; if not, consult the national journal or national IP office for complete records.
